title: Monotonicity of the Bernoulli restriction probability
statement:
Fix a parameter $p \in [0,1]$, and for a predicate $E$ on restrictions of $n$ variables write $\bbP_p[E]$ for the probability that $E$ holds under a Bernoulli($p$) random restriction. If $A$ and $B$ are predicates on restrictions such that $A(\rho)$ implies $B(\rho)$ for every restriction $\rho$, then
\[
  \bbP_p[A] \le \bbP_p[B].
\]
hypotheses_covered: A ρ implies B ρ for every restriction ρ
replaced:
Let $p\in[0,1]$ and let $A,B$ be predicates on restrictions. If $A(\rho)$ implies $B(\rho)$
for every restriction $\rho$, then
\[
  \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,p\,A \le \mathrm{bernoulliRestrProb}\,p\,B .
\]
